race.name: GFNY Pérez Zeledón
race.tagline: A fast 115-kilometer Costa Rican course that saves 1,903 meters of climbing and an eight-kilometer ascent for the back half.

vitals.location: Pérez Zeledón, San José Province, Costa Rica
vitals.start_format: Mass-start competitive long course with chip timing
vitals.registration: Online through the official GFNY race site
vitals.feed_zones: Official GFNY aid stations with hydration, food, technical, and medical support
vitals.cutoff_time: See current race guide and official course rules
route_options: Recreational medium route: see official race site

climate.description: The course moves from fast lowland roads into the green mountain terrain around Pérez Zeledón. Riders should prepare for strong sun, warm conditions, and the possibility of changing weather around the climbs.

terrain.primary: Fast opening into sustained tropical climbing
terrain.surface: Paved urban, main-road, and mountain roads around San Isidro del General and Pérez Zeledón.
features: A controlled rollout followed by very fast flat sections
Several sustained climbs beginning near Pacuar
An eight-kilometer ascent from 617 to 965 meters after kilometer 70
A false-flat and descending return to Hotel del Sur

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: A demanding and unusually well-defined inaugural course with nearly 1,900 meters of climbing in 115 kilometers. First-edition execution and limited established prestige keep it below Tier 1.

key_climbs: Santa Teresa de Cajón: approximately eight kilometers from 617 to 965 meters
climb_profile.profile_type: Fast opening into sustained tropical climbing
climb_profile.king_of_mountain: The eight-kilometer Santa Teresa de Cajón ascent after kilometer 70, where the route gains roughly 348 meters before the late return.

course_description.character: Pérez Zeledón opens fast enough to tempt riders into overspending, then introduces the climbs that account for 1,903 meters of total gain. The key eight-kilometer ascent arrives after kilometer 70, followed by false-flat terrain and a descending return, so pacing and heat management have to survive the early speed.
course_description.signature_challenge: Reaching the eight-kilometer Santa Teresa de Cajón climb with enough fuel and restraint to hold steady power.

logistics.airport: Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) is the main international gateway; Pérez Zeledón requires an overland transfer from the San José area.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in or near San Isidro del General and confirm race-hub access to Hotel del Sur in the current race guide.
logistics.transport: Use official race-week instructions for packet pickup, start access, and bike transport.
logistics.food: San Isidro del General has restaurants and markets; carry practiced fluids and carbohydrates because the decisive climbing comes after the fast opening.

history.origin_story: GFNY announced its return to Costa Rica in March 2026 with a new host in Pérez Zeledón and a start and finish at Hotel del Sur.
notable_moments: 2026: GFNY announces the new Pérez Zeledón event
history.reputation: An unproven but serious inaugural race whose published climbing makes it more than a destination fondo.

biased_opinion.summary: Pérez Zeledón is designed to bait you. The opening roads invite race speed, but almost 1,900 meters of climbing and the main ascent after kilometer 70 punish anyone who treats the first hour as free. This is a pacing race disguised as a fast one.
weaknesses: Heat and mountain weather add uncertainty
Overland travel from the main airport
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A legitimate climbing target for riders who can stay patient through a fast opening and still race after kilometer 70.

final_verdict.one_liner: A fast 115-kilometer Costa Rican course that saves 1,903 meters of climbing and an eight-kilometer ascent for the back half.
final_verdict.should_you_race: A legitimate climbing target for riders who can stay patient through a fast opening and still race after kilometer 70.
final_verdict.alternatives: GFNY Villavicencio for a longer Colombian mountain course, or GFNY Cozumel for a flatter tropical race.
